newsitem.title: USA: Politicians have plan to lure Dodgers home.
newsitem.headline: Politicians have plan to lure Dodgers home.

text.p: The Dodgers left Brooklyn four decades ago, but some locals have never stopped hoping the baseball team will come back one day.
Democratic Reps. Charles Schumer and Jerrold Nadler announced legislation Monday that would change the rules of major league baseball and open a tiny window of opportunity to bring the Dodgers home.
Called the Freedom of Movement for Baseball Teams Act of 1997, the bill would strike down rules set in 1922 governing baseball's anti-trust immunity on the movement of teams.

As the rules exist, three-quarters of all National League owners and a majority of American League owners would have to approve a move by the Dodgers back to Brooklyn. And the owners of the New York Yankees and the New York Mets could veto a plan to move another team into the market.
"If we can achieve our dream of finding an investor to bring the Dodgers home, we shouldn't let (Yankee owner) George Steinbrenner or anyone else stand in our way," said Schumer.
Owner Walter O'Malley broke countless hearts -- and made countless enemies -- when he moved the beloved Brooklyn Dogdgers to Los Angeles after the 1957 baseball season.
His son Peter O'Malley announced in January that the team is up for sale. The franchise is expected to sell for more than $300 million.
Rupert Murdoch, whose media empire includes Fox Sports, has expressed interest in buying the team.
Brooklyn Borough President Howard Golden said he knows a wealthy former Brooklyn resident who wants to bid for the team. He did not identify the potential bidder.
Golden complained that O'Malley rejected a meeting on the possible move to Brooklyn. When he announced the sale, O'Malley said keeping the team in Los Angeles was a priority.
"Peter is the second generation of O'Malleys who have told Brooklyn to drop dead," Golden said.

A number of local politicians have adopted the Dodger cause, including New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani and Gov. George Pataki, who have appointed a panel to formulate a business deal to bring the team back.
